decisions.D-01: One `workspaces` entity + workspace_type ('artist_team'|'management'|'label'). Type drives defaults and UI, never authorization.
decisions.D-02: Roster and catalogue capabilities are independent flags, not exclusive types — one company can be both management and label without a second workspace.
decisions.D-03: A solo Artist Team may be created on demand and expanded later. NEVER auto-provisioned — explicitly rejects the buyer_orgs.is_personal pattern.
decisions.D-04: Management/Label workspaces are self-declared and created instantly but visibly UNVERIFIED. Verification is a separate auditable state. Explicitly NOT buyer_orgs' born-verified default (migration 080 D-14).
decisions.D-05: Roster claims are inert until the artist affirmatively accepts. Creating a workspace and naming an artist grants no data, visibility or access. Structural protection, not policy.
decisions.D-06: Any Member may create any workspace type. Creation is not the control point — acceptance and verification are.
decisions.D-07: An Artist Team centers a named subject artist who must accept. Anyone may create one (e.g. a manager for their client) but it reaches nothing until the artist accepts.
decisions.D-08: Document-supported label master ownership automatically unlocks catalogue, metadata, readiness, registrations and delivery for those recordings. Clean-master DOWNLOAD remains a separately granted, logged capability — preserves custody D-01. A merely Claimed record grants nothing.
decisions.D-09: Separation runs two independent clocks: evidenced master ownership persists after the roster relationship ends; workspace-derived access ends. Artist keeps compositions, catalogue and personal projects.
decisions.D-10: A Label workspace may file a master-ownership claim on a version it cannot reach. It lands as D-02 'Claimed', notifies the artist/owner, is visible to both sides, and grants nothing.
decisions.D-11: Five workspace roles: Owner, Admin, Member, Contractor, Guest. They govern the WORKSPACE (invite, configure, roster, remove) — NOT project access, which comes from separate grants. Contractor is time-boxed, so membership needs an 'expired' state.
decisions.D-12: Invite by email. A pending seat exists immediately, grants nothing, and binds on signup + email verification. Reuses work_members' collaborator_id two-axis pattern and migration 177's SERVICE-ONLY find_auth_user_id_by_email. Never auto-provision an account.
decisions.D-13: Never-zero-owners enforced at the DB/service layer, not the UI. Ownership transfer = promote successor, then step down.
decisions.D-14: Removal ends future access immediately. Notes, uploads, approvals, diary entries, split-sheet parties, signatures and audit trail persist, attributed. Mirrors split_sheet_parties' create-time identity snapshot (018 D-19).
decisions.D-15: An artist may hold any number of roster relationships. Funūn NEVER enforces exclusivity — that is a contract term between parties, consistent with custody D-02's 'records, does not adjudicate'.
decisions.D-16: An agreement document is OPTIONAL to form a roster relationship (artist acceptance is real consent) but is a PREREQUISITE for authority-tier permissions. Moves the relationship from 'accepted' to 'document-supported' — the custody D-02 evidence ladder.
decisions.D-17: Effective and optional termination dates are tracked. Reaching termination auto-ends future workspace-derived access (per D-09 two-clock rule). Nothing is deleted; the record persists as history.
decisions.D-18: The artist may revoke any roster relationship unilaterally, immediately, with no approval. Access stops; record and history persist. Funūn is never the venue for the contractual argument and must never trap an artist in a disputed relationship.
decisions.D-19: Permissions are GRANULAR in the database (the only shape that expresses ~18 capabilities and survives RLS). The UI offers editable preset bundles. Nothing is hardcoded to a role name.
decisions.D-20: A grant attaches to the artist<->workspace RELATIONSHIP by default and may be narrowed or widened PER PROJECT.
decisions.D-21: TWO permission tiers. Operational (view summaries, metadata, Writer's Room, upload audio, invite collaborators, view split sheets, registrations) — artist grants alone. Authority (request signatures, approve releases, deliver assets, manage payouts, edit rights, act on behalf) — additionally requires a document-supported relationship per D-16.
decisions.D-22: Acting on behalf of an artist is ALWAYS attributed ('Alex (Rise Management, on behalf of Jordan)'). No view-as, no login-as, no impersonation of any kind.
decisions.D-23: The ARTIST holds the project record; a workspace reaches it through an attachment record. No owner_workspace_id column — vault_projects.user_id keeps its current meaning, so personal URLs/workflows are untouched and D-09 ('artist keeps their catalogue') is structural.
decisions.D-24: A workspace with the right grant MAY create a project for an artist. It is born held by the artist, with the diary recording who created it. Requires an already-accepted relationship. No transfer step, no orphan state.
decisions.D-25: Detachment severs the link only. Nothing moves, copies or is deleted. The workspace stops seeing the project EXCEPT recordings it owns of record (D-09). One project, one master, one home.
decisions.D-26: One canonical project, many views. A workspace 'catalogue' is a QUERY over attachments, never a copy. Same rows for artist and label, differing only by which fields the grant exposes.
decisions.D-27: A record a member performs on but does not hold appears on a separate read-only 'Appears on' shelf — extending Phase 21's 'Shared with me' lane, which already excludes shared projects from personal dashboard math.
decisions.D-28: CANONICAL RULE: vault_projects.user_id / works.user_id mean RECORD CUSTODY — who holds and administers the record in Funun — NEVER rights ownership. Rights always live on separate evidenced records (split sheets = composition; version ownership status = master, custody D-02). Stated explicitly in ACCOUNT-TYPES.md and The Playbook. No column rename.
decisions.D-29: Record custody MAY transfer, but only as a two-sided act: current holder offers, recipient accepts, diary records it permanently. Never unilateral.
decisions.D-30: Active workspace is carried in the URL path (/w/[workspaceId]/...) and RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE on every request from URL + authenticated user, never from client state. Tabs are naturally independent; personal routes keep existing URLs.
decisions.D-31: Wrong-context protection is BOTH: persistent visual workspace identity in the chrome AND a server-side re-check of acting context on every write. Upholds 'navigation visibility is not authorization'.
decisions.D-32: Management/Label landing = Roster and Activity as sibling tabs, roster default. Roster = state (readiness, missing info, outstanding approvals); Activity = events. Care required so the two never contradict.
decisions.D-33: Switching workspace is INSTANT and IN-SESSION for Members — one identity, one session, no re-auth. Funun Team Member accounts keep their existing hard sign-out/sign-in boundary unchanged, because staff is a separate identity, not a workspace.
decisions.D-34: CANONICAL TERMINOLOGY: schema and permission model use NEUTRAL language — 'member', 'roster member', 'subject member'. No artist-specific language in any structure. 'Artist Team' survives as a UI/product name only. Roster cards label people by their actual professional role (Producer, Songwriter, Engineer). Amends D-07's wording; its substance (a centred subject who must accept) is unchanged.
decisions.D-35: A management/label roster may hold ANY Member — artists, producers, songwriters, engineers — with no schema fork. One roster table; the CARD is role-aware (artist: release readiness; producer: placements + pending splits; songwriter: works + splits + PRO/registration; engineer: credits + sessions). D-27's 'Appears on' shelf is more central for producers/engineers than for artists.
decisions.D-36: The RIGHTS HOLDER declares the scope of authority they are granting and attaches the agreement as supporting evidence. The grant is their explicit act; the document is proof of why. Funun NEVER parses or interprets the file.
decisions.D-37: NEVER the word 'verified' for anything Funun merely stored. State it by showing PROVENANCE: who uploaded, when, what it was declared to support, whether Funun witnessed the signature. Counsel reviews final labels.
decisions.D-38: Documents about one member live once in THEIR Contract Locker; the workspace views what its grant permits. Genuinely workspace-level papers get a workspace shelf.
decisions.D-39: On document expiry, authority-tier permissions lapse automatically; operational access persists until the relationship ends per D-17.
decisions.D-40: Clean-master download, private rights identifiers and earnings visibility stay operational tier but are EXCLUDED from every preset bundle, ticked individually, every use logged.
decisions.D-41: Rights-information edits (PRO, IPI, publisher, SoundExchange) are PROPOSE-ONLY; the member confirms. Reuses Phase 19 confirmable pre-fill.
decisions.D-42: Payout and tax information is STRUCTURALLY EXCLUDED. No permission, bundle or tier can expose it to a workspace.
decisions.D-43: Workspace membership NEVER touches split sheets. This phase adds NO new path into a split sheet; it restates the existing rule in docs.
decisions.D-44: A workspace is its own billable entity with its own plan. New org-billing model (subscriptions today is per-user UNIQUE).
decisions.D-45: The workspace plan covers work done through the workspace; a member's personal plan governs solo work. No silent consumption of personal credits.
decisions.D-46: On lapse the workspace goes READ-ONLY. Relationships, attachments, grants, evidence and audit trail persist. A billing event must never destroy rights evidence.
decisions.D-47: Free during beta; seat/roster/storage/AI/e-sign counters TRACKED but NOT ENFORCED so pricing is decided on evidence.
decisions.D-48: Workspace-derived access reaches RLS by extending the existing SECURITY DEFINER helpers with a workspace branch — no policy rewrite. Follows 064/078/136. Watch per-row performance.
decisions.D-49: Server-side SUBSET CHECK on every grant AND re-check on use, so a grant cannot outlive the granter's own access.
decisions.D-50: Every workspace-context action records actor, workspace, subject member, permission relied on, timestamp. Append-only, visible to BOTH sides.
decisions.D-51: Invitations and roster claims are rate-limited per workspace, expire if unaccepted, and a member may BLOCK a workspace after refusing.
decisions.D-52: project_members is UNTOUCHED. Workspace access is a separate path through the same helpers. Phase 21 sharing unchanged.
decisions.D-53: Nothing automatic for existing manager/A&R members. No workspace provisioned for anyone. Zero migration risk.
decisions.D-54: This phase neither reads, writes nor removes member_type, industry_roles or capability_grants. That is its own audited cleanup phase.
decisions.D-55: Cohort-scoped SERVER-SIDE FLAG following the Song Passport pilot pattern. Personal workflows and URLs unchanged outside the cohort. NOTE: no kill switch selected — recorded as a risk/recommendation for planning.

open_followups: Placement of clean-master download, private rights identifiers (IPI/tax) and earnings visibility within the two-tier model — resolve in Areas 9 and 11 (user chose 2 tiers, not 3).
